mainTopic: The size of a מקוה and the ים של שלמה; the size and placement of a לחי, and the הלכה about רבי יוסי
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא that learns the minimum size of a מקוה from the פסוק: one אמה by one אמה, three אמות high, which the חכמים measured as ארבעים סאה. The גמרא uses this measure to check the claim that the ים של שלמה held 150 מקוואות. After working through square and round shapes, it concludes, following רמי בר יחזקאל, that the bottom three אמות were square and the top two were round. A פסוק saying the sea held 2,000 בת confirms this, and the 3,000 בת in another פסוק is explained as a heaped measure of dry goods. From this, אביי learns that a heap is one-third of the total, and a משנה in כלים supports him. A new משנה then sets the size of a לחי: ten טפחים tall and any width, while רבי יוסי requires three טפחים. The גמרא explains the plural לחיין, and adds rules about a לחי placed halfway into a מבוי and a לחי raised off the ground or set away from the wall. Finally, the הלכה about רבי יוסי is debated through conflicting reports and a retraction, and אביי answers: פוק חזי מאי עמא דבר.

steps.title: The verse teaches immersion in a body of water big enough for the whole body
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads 'במים' as מקוה water and 'כל בשרו' as water that covers the whole body at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In water' means in the water of a מקוה. 'All his flesh' means water that his whole body can go into at one time.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is reading two words from the פסוק about טבילה to learn what kind of water is needed and how much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'במים' tells us the water must be a gathered pool, a מקוה, not just any water. 'כל בשרו' adds a size requirement: the whole body must fit in the water at once. This sets up the next line, which turns that requirement into a number.

keyTerms.meaning: A gathered pool of water used for ritual immersion
'All his flesh': the whole body must be immersed
Goes into them, meaning the body enters the water fully

phrases.english: 'In water' means in the water of a ritual bath.
phrases.notes: From the פסוק 'ורחץ את בשרו במים' (ויקרא טו:טז).

phrases.english: 'All his flesh' means:
water that his entire body can go into at once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began on the previous amud, explaining the source for the size of a מקוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טבילה must be in a gathered body of water large enough for the whole body to enter at once.

steps.title: The minimum size of a מקוה: 1 by 1 by 3 אמות, or ארבעים סאה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the size of a body-sized pool as one אמה by one אמה, three אמות high, which the חכמים measured as ארבעים סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much water is that? One אמה by one אמה, three אמות high. The חכמים calculated that the water of a מקוה is forty סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא turns 'enough water for the whole body' into exact measurements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One by one by three equals three cubic אמות, and the חכמים set this volume as ארבעים סאה. The key number for the next steps is that one מקוה equals three cubic אמות. The גמרא will now use this number to test the claim about the ים של שלמה.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, a unit of length (about 18–24 inches)
A unit of volume; a מקוה needs 40 of them

steps.whatToRemember: One kosher מקוה equals 3 cubic אמות (1×1×3), which is ארבעים סאה. Every calculation that follows uses this number.

phrases.english: And how much is that?

phrases.aramaic: אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה בְּרוּם שָׁלֹשׁ אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: A cubit by a cubit, at a height of three cubits.
And the Sages calculated
that the water of a ritual bath is forty se'ah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the size requirement from step 1 into exact numbers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מקוה is at least 1×1×3 אמות, which is ארבעים סאה.

steps.title: The math does not work: the ים של שלמה is too big for 150 מקוואות
steps.stepSummary: The sea was 500 cubic אמות, but 150 מקוואות need only 450, so the earlier claim seems wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: How many מקוואות would the sea hold? The sea was 500 cubic אמות. 300 cubic אמות make 100 מקוואות, and 150 cubic אמות make 50 more. So 450 cubic אמות would be enough for 150 מקוואות. Why was the sea 500?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the 3-cubic-אמה measure to the ים של שלמה and finds that the numbers do not match the claim that it held 150 מקוואות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ים של שלמה was 10 by 10 אמות and 5 אמות high, which is 500 cubic אמות. At 3 cubic אמות per מקוה, 150 מקוואות need only 450. That leaves 50 cubic אמות unexplained, so the claim and the measurements seem to conflict.

phrases.english: How much do they amount to?
phrases.notes: Asks how many מקוואות the sea's volume really holds.

phrases.english: Five hundred cubic cubits.
phrases.notes: That's 10 by 10 by 5, from the description in מלכים א ז.

phrases.english: For three hundred, one hundred.
For one hundred fifty, fifty.
Four hundred fifty should be enough!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the מקוה measure from step 2 to test the earlier claim that the ים של שלמה held 150 מקוואות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ים של שלמה, measuring 500 cubic אמות, held exactly 150 מקוואות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 150 מקוואות × 3 cubic אמות = 450, not 500, so the volume and the count do not match.

steps.title: Answer: the sea was round, not square
steps.stepSummary: The 500 figure assumes a square shape, but the ים של שלמה was round, so its real volume was smaller.
steps.simpleTranslation: This calculation only works for a square. The sea that שלמה made was round.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 500 figure is wrong because it treats the sea as a square block, when it was actually round.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 10×10×5 is the volume of a square tank. A round tank 10 אמות across holds less water. So the real volume is less than 500, which might close the gap to 450.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only to; this is true only when

phrases.english: This applies to a square;
the sea that Solomon made was round.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 by correcting the shape assumed in the calculation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects a hidden assumption in the facts: the shape of the sea.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sea was a square block of 10×10×5 = 500 cubic אמות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sea was round, so its volume was less than 500.

steps.title: New problem: a round sea is now too small, only 125 מקוואות
steps.stepSummary: A circle is a quarter smaller than a square, so the round sea holds only 375 cubic אמות, which is 125 מקוואות, not 150.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, how much bigger is a square than a circle? By a quarter. So take a quarter off: from 400, take away 100, leaving 300, which is 100 מקוואות. From the other 100, take away 25, leaving 75, which is 25 מקוואות. That makes only 125 מקוואות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. If the sea was round, the math now gives too few מקוואות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A circle fills about three quarters of the square around it, so 500 drops to 375 cubic אמות. At 3 per מקוה, that is only 125 מקוואות. The answer of step 4 overcorrected: the volume went from too much (500) to too little (375). The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, consider; introduces a calculation that leads to a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: 'A square is larger than the circle by a quarter' means you subtract a quarter of the square's volume (500 → 375). Do not add a quarter to the circle. The גמרא splits 500 into 400 and 100 only to make the subtraction easy: 400 → 300 (100 מקוואות) and 100 → 75 (25 מקוואות).
steps.whatToRemember: Square shape: 500 cubic אמות, too much for 150 מקוואות. Round shape: 375 cubic אמות, only 125 מקוואות, too little. The גמרא still needs a shape that comes out to exactly 450.

phrases.english: Now, by how much is a square
larger than a circle? By a quarter.
For four hundred, take off one hundred,
phrases.notes: Taking 100 off 400 leaves 300 cubic אמות, which make 100 מקוואות.

phrases.english: for one hundred, take off twenty-five.
phrases.notes: Taking 25 off 100 leaves 75 cubic אמות, which make 25 מקוואות.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה הָווּ לְהוּ!
phrases.english: These amount to only one hundred twenty-five!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי, כַּמָּה מְרוּבָּע יָתֵר עַל הֶעָגוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4: making the sea round removes too much volume.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ים של שלמה was round.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A circle is a quarter smaller than a square, so 500 becomes 375 cubic אמות, which holds only 125 מקוואות instead of 150.

steps.title: The sea was square on the bottom and round on top
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל teaches that the bottom three אמות of the sea were square and the top two were round, which adds up to exactly 150 מקוואות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר יחזקאל taught: In the sea that שלמה made, the bottom three אמות were square, and the top two were round.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the math problem from step 5 with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says the sea was only partly round.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sea was 10 by 10 אמות. The square bottom (10×10×3) holds 300 cubic אמות, which is 100 מקוואות. The round top (10×10×2, minus a quarter) holds 150 cubic אמות, which is 50 מקוואות. Together that makes exactly 150.

phrases.english: Rami bar Yechezkel taught:
The sea that Shlomo made —
the three lower cubits were square,
phrases.notes: That's 10 by 10 by 3, or 300 cubic אמות, which is 100 מקוואות.

phrases.english: and the two upper ones were round.
phrases.notes: That's 200 minus a quarter, so 150 cubic אמות, which is 50 מקוואות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the 125-versus-150 problem from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the shape of the case: the sea was partly square and partly round.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole sea was round, so it held only 125 מקוואות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the top two אמות were round, so the total is exactly 150.
steps.whyThisMatters: It saves the claim that the sea held 150 מקוואות, which is what backs up the measurement of a מקווה as ארבעים סאה.

steps.title: Why not say only the top one cubit was round?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק forces the top to be round, but why must two אמות be round? Perhaps it was only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, you cannot say the opposite (round bottom, square top), because it is written 'its rim was round.' But say that only one אמה was round!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the exact split in רמי בר יחזקאל's ברייתא. Since only the rim must be round, maybe only the top single אמה was round.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'שפתו עגול' proves the top was round, but it does not say how much of it. If only one אמה were round, the volume would be 400 + 75 = 475 cubic אמות, which is more than 150 מקוואות. So the גמרא wants proof for the 3-and-2 split.

phrases.english: Granted that you cannot say the opposite —
since 'its rim was round' is written,
phrases.notes: The rim is at the top, so the top must be the round part.

phrases.english: but say only one (cubit was round)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the specific split given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר יחזקאל's claim that two upper אמות were round
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק only requires a round rim, so the round part could be smaller than two אמות. Nothing so far proves the 3/2 split.

steps.title: The verse says 2,000 בת, which is exactly 150 מקוואות
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the sea held 2,000 בת. A בת is 3 סאה, so the sea held 6,000 סאה, exactly 150 מקוואות. That only works with the 3/2 split.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot enter your mind, because it is written: 'It held two thousand בת.' How much is a בת? Three סאה, as it is written: 'a tenth of the בת from the כור.' So that comes to six thousand סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the one-אמה suggestion by proving from פסוקים that the sea held exactly 150 מקוואות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כור is 30 סאה, and a בת is a tenth of a כור, so a בת is 3 סאה. 2,000 בת × 3 = 6,000 סאה, and 6,000 ÷ 40 = 150 מקוואות. A one-אמה round top would hold more than that, so the split must be three square and two round.
steps.whatToRemember: 2,000 בת = 6,000 סאה = 150 מקוואות. This confirms the 3 square + 2 round shape.

phrases.english: That cannot enter your mind,
for it is written: 'It held two thousand bat.'
How much is a 'bat'? Three se'ah,
as it is written: 'a tenth of the bat from the kor,'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל מה:יד. A כור is 30 סאה, so a tenth of it is 3 סאה.

phrases.english: so it comes to six thousand se'ah.
phrases.notes: Divide 6,000 by 40 and you get 150 מקוואות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 with a volume proof from פסוקים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a פסוק that fixes the exact volume.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe only one אמה on top was round.
steps.terutzMaskana: The total volume is fixed at 6,000 סאה, which fits only the 3/2 split.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א ז:כו and יחזקאל מה:יד

steps.title: Another verse says 3,000 בת
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in דברי הימים says the sea held 3,000 בת, which contradicts the 2,000 used in the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'It held three thousand בת'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from step 8 with a different פסוק that gives a bigger number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sea held 3,000 בת, it would hold 9,000 סאה, which is 225 מקוואות, not 150. That would ruin the calculation that confirmed רמי בר יחזקאל.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
'It holds three thousand bat'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source used in step 8.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two פסוקים give different capacities (2,000 versus 3,000 בת), so the proof seems to be undermined.

steps.title: The 3,000 counts dry goods heaped above the rim
steps.stepSummary: The 3,000 בת measures dry goods piled up high above the rim. The 2,000 measures liquid, which is what counts for a מקווה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse refers to a heaped-up measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the two פסוקים: each one measures something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquid fills only up to the rim, which is 2,000 בת. Dry goods can be piled above the rim in a heap, which adds 1,000 more. Since a מקווה is water, the 2,000 figure is the one that counts, and the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: a heaped measure (piled above the rim)

steps.whatToRemember: The two numbers measure different things: 2,000 בת of liquid, 3,000 בת of heaped dry goods. The 150-מקוואות proof stands.

phrases.english: That (verse) refers to the heaped measure.
phrases.notes: That's dry goods piled up above the brim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two פסוקים: each refers to a different kind of measure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים contradict each other about the sea's capacity.
steps.terutzMaskana: 2,000 בת is the liquid capacity, and 3,000 בת is the heaped dry capacity.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ים של שלמה held 150 מקוואות of water, which confirms the ארבעים סאה measurement.

steps.title: אביי learns that a heaped load adds one-third
steps.stepSummary: אביי draws a general rule from the last answer: the heaped part of dry goods is one-third of the total.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that the heaped portion (גודשה) is one-third.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the answer from step 10 and turns it into a general rule about how much extra fits in a container when dry goods are heaped up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sea held 2,000 בת of liquid and 3,000 בת of heaped dry goods. The extra 1,000 is one-third of the full heaped amount of 3,000. So whenever dry goods are heaped, one-third of the total sits above the rim.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it. Introduces a conclusion drawn from what was just said.
The heap. The extra amount of dry goods piled above the rim.

steps.confusionAlert: The one-third is a third of the heaped total (1,000 out of 3,000). It is not a third of the liquid amount. Compared to the liquid amount, the extra is one-half.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Learn from it:
this heaped surplus is one-third.
phrases.notes: 2,000 of liquid becomes 3,000 when heaped, so 1,000 of the 3,000 is the heap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general measurement rule from the answer in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When dry goods are heaped, the heap above the rim is one-third of the heaped total (2,000 liquid → 3,000 heaped).

steps.title: A משנה in כלים supports the one-third rule
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in כלים says that 40 סאה of liquid equals two כור (60 סאה) of dry goods. That matches אביי's one-third rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned in a משנה: A carriage, a box, a cupboard, a straw barrel, a reed barrel, and the water tank of an Alexandrian ship are all טהור (cannot become impure). This is true even though they have bottoms, because they hold 40 סאה of liquid, which is two כור of dry goods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that backs up אביי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One כור is 30 סאה, so two כור is 60 סאה. The משנה says a container that holds 40 סאה of liquid holds 60 סאה of dry goods. The extra 20 is one-third of 60, which matches אביי exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: And we also learned (in a משנה). Introduces support from a משנה.
Bottoms. Shows the item can hold things, which would normally make it a vessel.
A large measure equal to 30 סאה

steps.whyThisMatters: These items are טהור because a container this large (40 סאה) is no longer treated as a 'vessel' for טומאה. The math in the same line is what proves אביי's rule.

phrases.english: And we also learned:
a carriage, a box, and a cupboard,
a round straw barrel and a round reed barrel,
and the water tank of an Alexandrian ship,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן שׁוּלַיִם
phrases.english: even though they have bottoms,
since they hold forty se'ah of liquid,
which is two kor of dry goods,
phrases.notes: Two כור is 60 סאה; going from 40 up to 60 is that one-third surplus.

phrases.english: they are ritually pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's inference with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule that a heaped measure is one-third of the total
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in כלים: 40 סאה of liquid equals two כור (60 סאה) of dry goods
steps.whatToRemember: Liquid to heaped dry goods is 2 to 3 (2,000 to 3,000 בת; 40 to 60 סאה). This closes the discussion of שלמה's sea.

steps.title: New משנה: the size of side posts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets the minimum size of a לחי: ten טפחים tall, with any width or thickness. רבי יוסי requires a width of three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The side posts the חכמים spoke of must be ten טפחים tall. Their width and thickness can be any amount. רבי יוסי says: their width must be three טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us how big a side post must be to permit carrying in an alley (מבוי).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The height must be ten טפחים, and on this everyone agrees. The disagreement is only about width. The תנא קמא says any width works, while רבי יוסי requires three טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה. The start of the משנה text.
Side posts (plural of לֶחִי). Upright posts placed at the alley entrance.
Any amount at all, even very small

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the plural word לחיין. The גמרא will ask about this right away.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The side posts that they spoke of,
their height is ten handbreadths,
and their width and thickness can be any amount.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: רׇחְבָּן שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: their width is three handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the sea discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לחי must be ten טפחים tall. According to the תנא קמא it may be any width; according to רבי יוסי it must be three טפחים wide.

steps.title: Does the plural mean the משנה follows רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the plural לחיין shows the unattributed משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who requires two side posts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding 'the side posts they spoke of': Shall we say this unattributed משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who said we need side posts, meaning two of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the plural word in the משנה secretly takes the side of רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier משנה records a debate: רבי אליעזר requires two side posts, while the חכמים say one is enough. If this unattributed משנה (סתם משנה) says 'side posts' in the plural, it may be following רבי אליעזר. That would be a problem, because the הלכה normally follows an unattributed משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? Introduces a suggested inference, often a problematic one.
An unattributed ruling. A משנה stated with no name attached.

phrases.english: GEMARA: 'The side posts that they spoke of,' etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the משנה.

phrases.english: Shall we say we learned an unattributed ruling following Rabbi Eliezer,
who said we require side posts (two)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the plural wording of the new משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the plural לחיין means the סתם משנה follows רבי אליעזר's view that two side posts are required.

steps.title: The plural means side posts in general
steps.stepSummary: No. 'Side posts' refers to all side posts in the world, not two in one alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What does 'side posts' mean? Side posts in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the plural word does not mean two posts per alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the plural because it is describing every side post anywhere. Each alley may still need only one. So the משנה can follow the חכמים.

phrases.english: No. What is meant by 'side posts'?
Side posts in general.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural refers to side posts in general, so the משנה does not require two per alley.

steps.title: Then the cross beam משנה should also use the plural
steps.stepSummary: If the plural just means 'in general,' the earlier משנה about the קורה should also have said קורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the משנה about the cross beam should also say 'cross beams,' and we would explain: what does 'cross beams' mean? Cross beams in general!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer by comparing it to the earlier משנה, which used the singular קורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה about the cross beam spoke in the singular. If a תנא uses the plural just to mean 'in general,' he should have done the same there. Since he used the singular for the beam, the plural here still looks meaningful, as if it means two.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. Introduces a challenge built on the previous answer.
Cross beam. Placed across the top of an alley entrance.

phrases.english: If so, the cross beam too:
let it teach 'cross beams,'
and what are 'cross beams'? Cross beams in general!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the plural לחיין simply means side posts in general
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The parallel משנה about the cross beam uses the singular. If plural wording only meant 'in general,' it would have said קורות. So the different wording suggests the plural here is meant literally.

steps.title: The plural means 'those side posts they argued about'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses the plural לחיין to point to the לחיין in the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and חכמים. It is not a ruling that two are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: those side posts that רבי אליעזר and חכמים argued about must be ten טפחים tall, and their width and thickness can be any amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from the last step: if the plural only means 'side posts in general,' why did the משנה about the קורה not say קורות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural is a reference back to the לחיין in the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר (two) and חכמים (one). Since there was no such argument about the number of קורות, the משנה about the קורה had no reason to use the plural. So the plural still does not prove the משנה follows רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (the גמרא re-reads the text)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
Those side posts about which there was a disagreement
between Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages,
their height is ten handbreadths,
and their width and thickness can be any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from step 16
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural is unexplained unless the משנה follows רבי אליעזר's view that two are needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural points to the לחיין in the known מחלוקת, so it fits חכמים as well.

steps.title: How small is 'any amount'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the real minimum behind the phrase 'any amount.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is 'any amount'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. It wants to know what 'any width' means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Any amount' sounds as if there is no minimum at all. The גמרא wants a concrete measure so we know what counts as a valid לחי.

phrases.english: And how much is 'any amount'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies a phrase in the reading given in step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical minimum width and thickness of a לחי

steps.title: Even as thin as a coat string
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that even a לחי as thin as the string of a coat is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: even as thin as the string of a coat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers the question with a ברייתא. A לחי as thin as a coat string is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Any amount' really means almost nothing. A string-thin post works, as long as it is ten טפחים tall.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya taught:
Even like the string of a coat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even the thickness of a coat string is enough
steps.whatToRemember: According to חכמים, a לחי must be ten טפחים tall, and its width can be tiny, even as thin as a coat string.

steps.title: A side post placed halfway into the alley
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a לחי is placed halfway into a מבוי, only the inner half is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if one made a side post for half an alley, he has only half the alley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a לחי placed in the middle of a מבוי instead of at the entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לחי works only from where it stands inward. The outer half, past the לחי, stays without a fix.

keyTerms.meaning: An alley that opens to the public domain

phrases.english: It was taught: one who made a side post for half an alley
has only half the alley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic about where a לחי is placed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לחי placed halfway into a מבוי permits only the inner half

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that it is obvious the outer half is not permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Why would it need to say something so obvious?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of course the part outside the לחי gets no help from it. A ברייתא should not bother teaching that.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that only half the מבוי is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling has no new teaching

steps.title: Read it as: he does get the inner half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-reads the ברייתא as a positive ruling: the inner half is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: he has half the alley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes the wording of the ברייתא. Its point is that the inner half is permitted, not that the outer half is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the stress is on what is allowed. One may carry in the inner half even though the entrance itself has no לחי.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
He has half the alley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא teaches the obvious point that the outer half is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches that the inner half is permitted.

steps.title: That is also obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that permitting the inner half is just as obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading as well. Of course the area inside the לחי is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner half is fully surrounded and has a לחי, so it should clearly be permitted. The ברייתא still seems to teach nothing new.

phrases.english: This too is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The re-read ruling that the inner half is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This ruling also has no new teaching

steps.title: No worry that he will use the whole alley
steps.stepSummary: The new point is that we do not forbid the inner half out of fear that people will carry in the whole מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said we should worry he will come to use the whole alley, so it teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real teaching. One might have forbidden even the inner half as a safeguard, so the ברייתא tells us that no such גזירה applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone carrying in the inner half might keep going into the outer half by mistake. The ברייתא teaches that חז״ל did not make a גזירה for this, so the inner half stays permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: The new teaching is not about where the לחי works. It is that we do not add a safeguard that would forbid the inner half.

phrases.english: You might have said:
let us be concerned that perhaps he will come
to use all of it;
it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forbid even the inner half in case he carries in the whole מבוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no such concern, so the inner half is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: A לחי placed halfway in permits the inner half. חז״ל did not forbid it out of fear that people would carry in the outer half.

steps.title: A side post raised off the ground or set away from the wall is worthless
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a לחי three טפחים above the ground, or three טפחים away from the wall, does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if one made a side post for an alley and raised it three טפחים from the ground, or set it three טפחים away from the wall, he has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule about where a לחי must stand. A gap of three טפחים below it, or beside it, makes it invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below three טפחים, the rule of לבוד treats a gap as closed. A gap of three טפחים is too big, so the לחי is not connected to the ground or to the wall.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If one made a side post for an alley
and raised it three handbreadths from the ground,
or set it three handbreadths away from the wall,
he has not done anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New rule about where a לחי must be placed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gap of three טפחים from the ground or from the wall makes a לחי invalid

steps.title: Even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees, because goats can pass below
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who applies לבוד up to four טפחים, would not apply it to a gap at the bottom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says we apply לבוד, that is only above. Below, since it is a partition that goats can pass through, he did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers a question before anyone asks it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows gaps of less than four טפחים, so why should three be a problem? רבא explains that this is only true for gaps higher up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Young goats can slip through a gap of three טפחים at the bottom, so it cannot be treated as closed. Higher up, nothing passes through, so even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's wider לבוד only works there.

keyTerms.meaning: Treating a small gap as closed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that לבוד is not a fixed number alone. Even the wider opinion does not apply it where animals can actually pass through.

phrases.english: Even according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
who said we apply the rule of 'connected,'
that applies only above,
but below,
since it is a partition
that young goats pass through,
he did not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and defends רבא's ruling in step 25 against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a gap of three טפחים is לבוד, so the לחי should be valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: לבוד up to four טפחים applies only above, not at the bottom where goats can pass.
steps.whatToRemember: A לחי must touch the ground and the wall, with a gap of less than three טפחים. At the bottom, even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יוסי's view in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's view from the משנה, that a לחי must be three טפחים wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: their width must be three טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה. It quotes רבי יוסי to set up the ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי disagrees with the 'any width' rule we just learned. This quote prepares the הלכה about his view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
their width is three handbreadths.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר רׇחְבָּן שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה quoted in step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי requires a לחי to be three טפחים wide

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules against רבי יוסי both about salt brine and about לחיין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: the הלכה is not like רבי יוסי, not about brine and not about side posts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes שמואל's ruling that we do not follow רבי יוסי. The next steps question whether this ruling really covers לחיין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל rejects רבי יוסי in two places at once: making salt brine on שבת, and the width of a לחי. Whether this ruling really covers לחיין is questioned in the next steps, and the practical answer comes only in step 39.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's ruling rejects רבי יוסי on both brine and לחיין, but the following steps dispute the לחיין part.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is not like Rabbi Yosei,
not about brine and not about side posts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the view quoted in step 27
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל rules against רבי יוסי on both brine and לחיין. The later steps question this ruling as it applies to לחיין.

steps.title: You only told us about brine, not about side posts
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא points out that the ruling against רבי יוסי was taught to them only for brine, not for לחיין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא said to him: About brine you told us the הלכה is not like רבי יוסי. About side posts, you did not tell us that.
steps.whatsHappening: A student reminds his teacher that the teacher only ruled against רבי יוסי about salt brine (הילמי), and never mentioned לחיין. This sets up a discussion about whether לחיין follow the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The student is hinting that the teacher's memory is off: the ruling against רבי יוסי may not cover לחיין at all. If so, the הלכה might actually follow רבי יוסי about לחיין, so a לחי would need to be three טפחים wide.

keyTerms.meaning: Salt brine (a fish-and-salt liquid), the other case where רבי יוסי has a position
Side posts placed at the entrance of a מבוי

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on רבי יוסי. It is a question about what the teacher originally taught. The student is saying the ruling was only about brine.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chinana said to him:
About brine you told us (that the halacha is not like Rabbi Yosei),
but about side posts you did not tell us!
phrases.notes: Left unsaid: so maybe the הלכה does follow רבי יוסי about side posts.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהֵילְמֵי אֲמַרְתְּ לַן, בִּלְחָיַיִן לָא אֲמַרְתְּ לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the scope of the ruling against רבי יוסי given in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did the ruling against רבי יוסי really include לחיין, or only brine?

steps.title: Why should brine and side posts be different?
steps.stepSummary: The teacher (some explain: רב יוסף) asks: the חכמים disagree with רבי יוסי in both cases, so why should the ruling differ?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about brine? There, the חכמים disagree with him. With side posts too, the חכמים disagree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The teacher pushes back: in both cases רבי יוסי stands alone against the חכמים, so both cases should get the same ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal rule is that a single תנא who argues with the majority does not set the הלכה. Since רבי יוסי is in the minority in both cases, there seems to be no reason to rule against him for brine but follow him for לחיין.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (a challenge to a distinction)

phrases.english: What is different about brine?
There the Sages disagree with him,
and with side posts as well, the Sages disagree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction suggested in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that לחיין might follow רבי יוסי while brine does not
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases have the same setup: one תנא against the majority. So they should get the same result.

steps.title: Side posts are different because רבי agrees with רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא answers that for לחיין, רבי (יהודה הנשיא) holds like רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Side posts are different, because רבי stands with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The student explains what makes the two cases different: in the case of לחיין, רבי agrees with רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבי joins רבי יוסי, he is no longer a lone voice. The combined weight of רבי and רבי יוסי makes it possible for the הלכה to follow them about לחיין, even though it does not follow רבי יוסי about brine.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands with him / holds like him

phrases.english: He said to him: Side posts are different,
because Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) holds like him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי לְחָיַיִן, מִשּׁוּם דְּקָאֵי רַבִּי כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases (who supports רבי יוסי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases are the same: רבי יוסי is alone against the חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: For לחיין, רבי agrees with רבי יוסי, so the הלכה may follow him there.

steps.title: רב רחומי's version: not like רבי יוסי in either case
steps.stepSummary: רב רחומי teaches that רב said the הלכה is not like רבי יוסי, neither for brine nor for לחיין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב רחומי taught it this way: רב יהודה son of רב שמואל בר שילת said in the name of רב: The הלכה is not like רבי יוסי, not about brine and not about side posts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the ruling, which says clearly that the הלכה is not like רבי יוסי in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version leaves no room for the distinction from step 31. According to it, a לחי of any small width works and does not need three טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught it this way (gives a different version)
The הלכה is not (like this view)

phrases.english: Rav Rechumi taught it this way:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל [בַּר שִׁילַת] מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel [bar Shilat], said in the name of Rav:
The halacha is not like Rabbi Yosei,
neither about brine nor about side posts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the ruling that rejects the distinction of step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, the הלכה is not like רבי יוסי, neither for brine nor for לחיין.

steps.title: Did you really say that?
steps.stepSummary: Someone asks רב יהודה whether he really said this ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Did you say this?
steps.whatsHappening: Later, the speaker is asked to confirm that he really taught this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question checks whether the ruling in step 32 is authentic. Its answer will affect whether we accept this version.

phrases.english: Someone said to him: Did you say (this)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to verify the ruling of step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the speaker actually taught the ruling against רבי יוסי

steps.title: He answers: No
steps.stepSummary: The speaker denies saying the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: No.
steps.whatsHappening: The speaker answers that he did not say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His denial seems to cancel the ruling in step 32. But the next step will show that he really did say it and later changed his mind.

phrases.english: He said to them: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.

steps.title: רבא swears that he did say it
steps.stepSummary: רבא swears that the speaker did say the ruling, and that רבא learned it from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: By God! He said it, and I learned it from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא strongly rejects the denial. He swears that he heard this ruling directly from the speaker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'No' did not mean the ruling was never said. It means the speaker took it back. So both facts are true: he once taught it, and now he no longer holds by it.

keyTerms.meaning: By God! (an oath used to stress that something is true)

phrases.english: Rava said: By God!
He said it, and I learned it from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the denial of step 34.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the ruling was never said
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא heard it himself, so the speaker must have said it and later retracted.

steps.title: Why did he retract?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the speaker changed his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason he retracted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what made him take back his ruling. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he once ruled against רבי יוסי, something must have convinced him to change. The גמרא wants to know what it was.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted / took back his view

phrases.english: And what is the reason he retracted it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the retraction established in step 35.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he took back his ruling against רבי יוסי

steps.title: Because רבי יוסי's reasoning is with him
steps.stepSummary: He retracted because of the principle 'רבי יוסי נימוקו עמו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because רבי יוסי's reasoning is with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that he changed his mind because of a known rule: רבי יוסי always has strong reasons, so we follow him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'נימוקו עמו' means רבי יוסי's opinions are carefully reasoned. Because of this, the הלכה follows him even against the majority. That is why the ruling against him was taken back.

keyTerms.meaning: His reasoning is with him (his views are well-grounded, so the הלכה follows him)

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling against רבי יוסי was said and then retracted, because 'רבי יוסי נימוקו עמו'.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'רבי יוסי נימוקו עמו' is a general rule for deciding הלכה that is used throughout ש״ס.

phrases.english: Because Rabbi Yosei's reasoning is with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He retracted because of the principle that רבי יוסי נימוקו עמו.

steps.title: So what is the practical הלכה?
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן asks אביי what the הלכה actually is about the width of a לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנן said to אביי: What is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: After so many conflicting versions, a student asks אביי for the bottom line. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The versions disagree: one ruling against רבי יוסי, one retracted, and one distinction based on רבי. So the student asks how people should actually act.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Chanan said to Abaye:
What is the halacha?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a practical ruling after the conflicting versions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical הלכה about the width of a לחי

steps.title: Go out and see what the people do
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the custom of the people decides the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go out and see what the people are doing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי does not give a ruling from the sources. He tells the student to look at the common practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the sources are unclear, the established custom of the Jewish people shows the הלכה. One explanation is that people commonly use a לחי of minimal width, which means they do not follow רבי יוסי's three טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: What the people are doing (common practice)

steps.whatToRemember: For the width of a לחי, the practice follows the common custom: a narrow לחי is used, not three טפחים.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'פוק חזי מאי עמא דבר' is a well-known tool: when a הלכה is unclear, accepted public custom decides it.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go out and see
what the people are doing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Follow the common practice of the people.

steps.title: Another version: the question was about the ברכה on water
steps.stepSummary: Some say אביי's answer was given about a different מחלוקת: which ברכה to say before drinking water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this exchange about the following: One who drinks water because he is thirsty says 'שהכל נהיה בדברו'. רבי טרפון says: 'בורא נפשות רבות וחסרונן על כל מה שבראת'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that some people place the 'go see what the people do' exchange on a different topic. It first quotes that topic: an argument about the ברכה for drinking water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the ברכה before drinking water is שהכל. רבי טרפון says it is בורא נפשות. This version sets up the same question and answer, but on this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it on this (a different case)
'By Whose word all things came to be' (the שהכל ברכה)
'Who creates many forms of life' (a ברכה)

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי טרפון uses בורא נפשות as the ברכה said before drinking. It is not the after-ברכה it is commonly known as today.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on this:
One who drinks water for his thirst says:
'By Whose word all things came to be.'
Rabbi Tarfon says:
'Who creates many living beings and their needs,
for all that You have created.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another placement for the exchange of steps 38-39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת: the תנא קמא says שהכל before drinking water, and רבי טרפון says בורא נפשות.

steps.title: What is the הלכה for the water ברכה?
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רב חנן asks אביי which ברכה is the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן said to אביי: What is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: In this version, the question to אביי is about which ברכה to say on water. This sets up the same answer as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is now about the תנא קמא against רבי טרפון, instead of the width of a לחי.

phrases.english: Rav Chanan said to Abaye:
What is the halacha?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the ruling on the מחלוקת quoted in step 40.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ברכה is said before drinking water

steps.title: Go see what the people do (people say שהכל)
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives the same answer: follow the common practice, which is to say שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go out and see what the people are doing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי again sends the questioner to look at common practice. Here, people say שהכל on water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this version, the 'go see' answer was given about the water ברכה, and the custom follows the תנא קמא (שהכל). Either way, the method is the same: when the הלכה is unclear, public custom decides it.
steps.whatToRemember: In this version, אביי's 'פוק חזי מאי עמא דבר' was said about the water ברכה, and the custom is to say שהכל.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go out and see
what the people are doing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 41.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practical הלכה follows public custom. For the water ברכה, that custom is שהכל.
